title: Rama Waits Out the Rains
hookLine: Rama, with every reason to rush, waits out the rains before the search for Sita: the Hindu year has seasons for waiting and for setting out
carry: the hindu year has a season for waiting
tomorrow: why did Bhishma wait for the sun?

cards: Rama has found an ally at last. Sugriva, the monkey king, has promised to send his armies to search for Sita. Then the sky turns.
Clouds pile over the mountains, the rivers swell, the roads turn to mud. Rama, whose wife has been carried off, has to sit on a mountainside and wait. Four months.

teach.b: In the Kishkindha book of Valmiki's Ramayana, Rama makes the call himself. The rainy months have begun, he tells Sugriva; this is no time to march.
Go home to your city, and when the month of Kartika comes, after the rains, make ready.
Then he spends the season in a cave on Mount Prasravana, watching the storms and aching for Sita, and the poet gives that waiting some of his loveliest verses.
When the clear autumn sky comes, sharad, and Lakshmana gives a forgetful Sugriva a sharp reminder, the search begins. Here's the teaching.
Hindu life keeps step with the year, and the year has seasons for waiting and seasons for going.
Many Hindus still keep chaturmas, the four months of the rains, when Vishnu is said to sleep on the cosmic serpent. Wandering monks traditionally stop traveling and stay in one place.
Many families hold no weddings until Vishnu wakes, on Prabodhini Ekadashi, in Kartika, the same month Rama waited for.

teach.h: A SEASON FOR WAITING, A SEASON FOR GOING
teach.b: Ayurveda reads the year the same way: ritucharya, the conduct of the season, a twin of the daily routine.
The Ashtanga Hridaya counts six seasons, the rains among them, and the Charaka Samhita says a person who knows what suits each season, in food and in activity, grows in strength.
Today, that's a different way to see a delay. Not every pause is a failure. In the Hindu year, some seasons are for staying put and gathering strength, and some are for setting out.
Rama, with every reason to rush, waited for his season.

how: Many Hindus keep chaturmas, the four months of the rains when Vishnu is said to sleep: wandering monks stay in one place, and many families hold no weddings until Prabodhini Ekadashi; Ayurveda's ritucharya adjusts food and activity season by season.

o: six turns of the year, each asking its own care
the weeks of the year set aside for fasting
four seasons, each ruled over by a different god

games.q: the year's round — tap the pairs.
p: the clear autumn, time to set out

s: in the Ramayana, Rama waits out the rains before the search for Sita
he tells Sugriva the rainy months are no time to march; make ready when Kartika comes.
Hindu families never let the calendar shape a wedding date
many avoid chaturmas and wait for Vishnu to wake on Prabodhini Ekadashi.
the Ashtanga Hridaya divides the year into four seasons
it names six, with the rains a season of their own.

games.q: Rama has an ally and every reason to rush. then the rains come. what does he do?
o: wait out the season, and set out in autumn.
games.why: he tells Sugriva the rains are no time to march. in the Hindu year, some seasons are for waiting, and some are for going.

practice: Notice the air on your skin, warm or cool, damp or dry, and the light where you are. Then turn inward: is this a season in your life for staying put, or for setting out? No fixing, just a weather report from the inside.
If you pray, you can offer the season you're in; many Hindus would say a name of Vishnu, like Om Namo Narayanaya.

wordCard.voice: The seasons. Ritu, a season, and ritucharya, the conduct that keeps step with it, from the rains to the clear autumn when Rama set out.

orig.note: Sanskrit ritucharya: ritu, season, and charya, conduct. The seasonal routine of the classical Ayurvedic texts.

carryVoice: Your line: the Hindu year has a season for waiting. Rama waited out the rains. Back tomorrow, same hill.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda 26–30 (Rama tells Sugriva the rainy months are no time to march and to make ready in Kartika; Rama's rainy season on Mount Prasravana; the coming of autumn)
Chaturmas: the four months from Devshayani to Prabodhini Ekadashi, when Vishnu is said to sleep; kept in Hindu calendar and vrata practice (monks' rainy-season retreat, weddings deferred)
Charaka Samhita, Sutrasthana 6.3 (strength and complexion grow for one who knows what suits each season in food and activity)
Ashtanga Hridaya, Sutrasthana 3.1–2 (the year in six seasons: shishira, vasanta, grishma, varsha, sharad, hemanta)
